chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Lu'lu'i, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, who said:

A man from our companions was in Medina, so he was constrained by severe constraints, and his state became difficult. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Go and take a shop in the market and spread out your spread sheet, and let there be with you a jug of water, and bind (it to) the door of your shop'.

He (the narrator) said, 'So the man did so, and remained like that for as long as Allah so Desired. Then travelling merchants from Egypt came over, so they cast their merchandise, each man from them with a known person of his and with a friend of his until the shops were filled up. There remained one man from them who could not come across a shop to cast his goods therein. So the people of the market said to him, 'Over there is a man with whom there is no problem, and there are no goods in his shop, if only you could cast your goods in his shop'. So he went to him and said to him, 'Will you cast my goods in your shop'. He said, 'Yes'. So the travelling merchants went out and the man went out along with them, and left the goods with him. So our companion sold them and sent his price to him. So whenever the travelling merchants of Egypt prepared to go out from Egypt, he would send his goods to him, so he would sell them and return its price to him. So when that man saw that, he stayed in Egypt and went on sending the goods to him, and equipped upon him'.

So when the departure of the caravan approached, a small amount of his goods remained with the man, and he disliked staying for it, so he said to our companion: 'I will leave this goods with you, you sell it and send its price to me'. He said, 'Yes'.

So the caravan went out and the man went out with them, and left the goods with him. So our companion sold it and sent its price to him. He said, 'So when the departure of the caravan of Egypt from Egypt prepared, he sent him merchandise, so he sold it and returned its price to him. So when that man saw that, he stayed in Egypt and went on sending the goods to him, and equipped upon him'.
He (the narrator) said: 'Thus he attained a lot of wealth and was enriched'.
ai.seo_question: How did a companion of the Imam overcome poverty through trade?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Imam’s practical wisdom in addressing economic distress by leveraging the social capital of trade networks; by offering a humble space for merchants to store goods, the companion transformed a simple shop into a hub of commerce. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on active participation in worldly affairs (mu'amalat) as a means of sustenance, provided one maintains integrity and avoids usury, contrasting with passive reliance on divine provision alone. The narrative underscores the virtue of facilitating others' livelihoods as a path to personal prosperity, a concept deeply rooted in Islamic economic ethics.
